In this case, the Petitioner has prayed the following in his Petition:
a. Issue notice of this application on the Respondent;
b. Grant and issue an order in the nature of a Writ of Mandamus compelling the
1't Respondent to make a recommendation to the Hon. President to cancel
Grant hearing Reference No. Gam/Pra/Miri/869 nominating Nelumdeni Devage
Sumanaseeli on 10/08/1997 and to nominate a suitable heir/heirs under the
Land Development Ordinance for the land in dispute to the said land after
impartial inquiry;
c. Grant an issue an order in the nature of a Writ of Mandamus compelling the 1st
Respondent or his agent/ representative/authorized officer to visit the land in
dispute, with notice to the Petitioners and ascertain the basis on which the 5th _
13th Respondents are residing on this land and take appropriate steps to make
recommendations to the President to cancel Grant bearing Reference
No.Gam/Pra/Miri/869;
d. For costs; and
e. For such other and further relief which Court shall seem meet.
The factual setting to this instant case is as follows;
The Petitioner's mother namely, Kumburudeni Devage Alice Nona was issued with a Grant (which
is marked as 'P2' to the Petition) to Lot No.363 in Cadastral Map No.510239 marked as 'P4' to the Petition. The said Kumburudeni Devage Alice had four children,
(i) Nelumdeni Devage Piyaseeli, (daughter).
Page 3 of 8
(ii) The Petitioner himself, (son). (iii) The 7th Respondent (son). (iv) Nelumdeni Devage Sumanaseeli, (daughter) namely the 11th Respondent.
The 1st daughter Piyaseeli had passed away and her Death Certificate is marked as 'P7' to the
Petition.
The Petitioner states that Kumburudeni Devage Alice, named the 11th Respondent as the

'nominated successor' under the said Grant. On 2002.04.09 Kumburudeni Devage Alice died and her Death certificate is at Page 56 of document marked as 'P1' to the Petition. The Petitioner states that the Petitioner and his family members have obtained Grants for lots 336, 337 and 338 of said Cadastral Map NO.510239 marked as 'P4'.

The Petitioner and his family members used a road way along the said Lot 363 in Cadastral Map No.510239 marked as 'P4'. The said Lot 363 is also at Page 103 of document marked as 'P1'. 'P1' is a partition action filed by the Petitioner who was the Plaintiff in such partition action. The Petitioner filed this partition action bearing No.422/P in the District Court of Atanagalle when the Defendants named in such partition action, (including the 5th to 14th respondents in this Writ Application) obstructed the Petitioner and his family members from using the said road way depicted in the Preliminary Plan No.1924 dated 2015.01.17. However, the said partition action
has now been withdrawn.
The Petitioner states that the Petitioner is praying, asking for a mandate in the nature of a
mandamus compelling the 1st Respondent to make a recommendation to the President to cancel
Grant bearing reference No. Gam/Pra/Miri/869 nominating the 11th Respondent AND also for a
mandamus compelling the 1't Respondent or his agent and representative authorized officer to
visit the land in dispute with notice to the Petitioners and ascertain the basis on which the 5th to
13th Respondents are residing on this land and take appropriate steps to make recommendations
to the President to cancel the Grant bearing Reference No.Gam/Pra/Miri/869.
The Petitioner states that as per section 104 of Land development ordinance; "The President may
make order cancelling the grant of a holding if he is satisfied that there has been a failure of
succession thereto either because there is no person lawfully entitled to succeed or because no
person so entitled is willing to succeed".
The 11th Respondent who is the nominated successor has failed to succeed to the land in dispute
and it is not a fact in dispute. The Petitioner states that the 11th Respondent never possessed the
land after the death of Kumburudeni Devage Alice. she was a resident elsewhere, namely at
'Radawadunna' and in proof the Petitioner has annexed the Electoral Registers are marked as
'P6a' to 'P6d' for the years 1990, 1991, 1992, 1993. The Petitioner states that, the given address is
the permanent address of the 11th respondent and accordingly she has sold a portion of the said
State land and had allowed her other relatives to occupy the said land.
The Petitioner states that in the said Preliminary Plan NO.1924 dated 2015.01.17

(1) in the house marked as c in Lot 1 (2) in the house marked as E in Lot 2 - the 12th and 13th Respondents are residing the 5th and 6th Respondents are residing the 8th Respondent is residing the 10th Respondent is residing the 9th Respondent is residing
(3) in the house marked as G & H in Lot 4 -(4) in the house marked as K in Lot 5 (5) in the house marked as L in Lot 6

Accordingly, it is submitted that the Grantor namely the 11th Respondent (who is the nominated successor to the Grant of Kumburudeni Devage Alice) nor her family members are residing at the particular disputed land and accordingly she has failed to succeed to the land in question.
The Petitioner states that in the document marked as 'P9' the Divisional Secretary has made the
observation that the 11th respondent had alienated land without prior approval of the Divisional
Secretary. The Petitioner emphasizes that the facts stated in 'P9' is not in dispute. Although the
11th Respondent has taken up such position during the argument that fact is in dispute, the 11th
Respondent had utterly failed to prove that such fact is in dispute.
In fact, the Preliminary Plan has corroborated the fact that outsiders have constructed a house in
Lot 1 in the house marked as C. Even the 1st Respondent had admitted this fact in their Statement
of Objections and documents marked as 'P9' and 'Pl0'. The Petitioner states that in 'P9' the 1st
Respondent states that number of the Deed of Gift, namely No.4188.
In the circumstances the Petitioner says that, such facts are not in dispute. The Petitioner further
states that the 11th respondent is now trying to evade such fact and misrepresent facts to this
Court as it would be unfavorable to them. The Petitioner has been able to prove that the 11th
respondent has alienated land without prior approval of the Divisional Secretary. Accordingly, the
burden then shifts to the 11th Respondent to prove that such fact is incorrect. But she has failed to
prove such fact does not exist other than her mere statement in the Objections.
It is emphasized by the Petitioner that, by document marked as 'P9' and'Pl0' it is manifestly clear
that the 1st Respondent had knowingly and willfully failed to take action to make recommendation
to the President to cancel the Grant of the 11th Respondent, when the 1st Respondent knew that
the 11th Respondent had failed to succeed to the land in question and that the 11th Respondent
had alienated land to 3rd parties and other relatives to construct houses in the land to the
question.
The Petitioner states that the Divisional Secretary had in fact tried to settle the dispute between
the parties but refused to inform the President that a Grant Holder is acting in contravention of
the conditions stipulated in the Grant and thereby acting in contravention of Section 19 (6) (b). If
a Holder of a Grant contravenes provisions in the Land Development Ordinance, and contravenes
the conditions of the holding, then such holding should be cancelled.
He further states that if the 11th Respondent is allowed to continue to act in contravention of the
conditions stipulated in the Grant, then there will be flood gates and the conditions in the Grant
and section 19 (6) (b) will be of no value. An owner to a holding can without any deterrent can
alienate lands as they please according to their whims and fancies.

The 6th, 7th, 8th ,9th ,11th and 13th Respondents in response to the aforesaid claims of the Petitioner
states that, the Petitioner is the eldest son of the family of Kamburudeni Devage Alice, and she
was the holder of the Grant of the relevant state land to this application. After tpe death of said
Kamburudeni Devage Alice on 19-04-2002, the Petitioner had made some legal and illegal acts to
grab the relevant land to this application. It is admitted in terms of the Petition of the Petitioner
that he possesses three lots of land marked as No.336, 337 and 338 of the Plan NO.510239 as
Grantee of state Lands.
The Respondents state that the Petitioner has made the allegation that the 11th Respondent has
alienated the land relevant to this application. They deny specifically the sale of the said state land
or part thereof by the said Kamburudeni Devage Alice or by the 11th Respondent who is the sister
of the Petitioner. All the houses referred in the Petition are the houses of the family members of
Kamburudeni Devage Alice. In other words, they say that all the above said Respondents are
family members of the said Kamburudeni Devage Alice. They all live peacefully on the said land
and it looks like the only obstruct is the Petitioner.
The state land cannot be claimed by inheritance. The Respondents state that there is no dispute
with regard to the relevant land to this application except the Petitioner. It is further stated that
the land referred therein is still a state land but there is that grant given to Kamburudeni Devage
Alic and subsequently to the 11th Respondent being the nominated successor of the said
Kamburudeni Devage Alice.
The Respondents further state that there was no 12 feet wide road on the relevant land leading to
the house of the Petitioner in terms of the survey plan submitted by the Petitioner. All the houses
are partly built and built by the members of the family of the said Kamburudeni Devage Alice
when she was living. The Respondents further state that there is no road depicted in the Plan
No.510239 on the land named and marked Lot No.363 which is the relevant land to this
application. It is illegal to build and construct a road on the state land. In the plan the right of way
has been allocated by the state very fairly to all the lots of the lands shown in the plan.
The 11th Respondent has indicated that she has not waived her rights on the relevant state land
and she has established her rights by coming into possession after the death of her mother said
Kamburudeni Devage Alice. The 11th Respondent being the nominated successor to the said state
land and she lives peacefully with her family members who are the above said 6th, 7th ,8th ,9th ,11th,
and 13th Respondents in a separate house. The Petitioner also has admitted and pleaded the
relationship with said Kamburudeni Devage Alice to the said Respondents who are in occupation in
the relevant state land.
It is an admitted fact in terms of pleadings that the 11th Respondent was nominated as the
successor of the said Kamburudeni Devage Alice to the relevant state land to this application as
the other three members of the family such as the Petitioner and the 7th Respondent had been
granted state lands in the same area in the same location.
A true copy of the grant of state land to the Petitioner is also produced marked "6Rln. It is further
stated that the Petitioner had been granted 03 lots of lands as per the plan No.510239 referred in
paragraph 09 of the Petition although the "6Rl" refers to one lot of land. The Respondents submit
Page 6 of8
that the Petitioner made undue pressure such as legal actions, and false complaints on them to
grab and use the relevant land as a road which is illegal, unlawful, unfair, impossible and
impracticable. The Petitioner has no right to enter relevant land to this application as the 11th
Respondent is the nominated successor of said Kamburudeni Devage Alice although the Petitioner
is the eldest in the family of the Kamburudeni Devage Alice.
The Respondents further state that the Petitioner was not in possession of the state land
concerned in this application. Therefore, the issue of ejection does not arise. The Respondent
argue that the Petitioner has misrepresented and suppressed the material facts of the issue
involved in this application before the Ministry of Lands and the public officers such as 1st, 2nd , and
the 14th Respondent to grab the land relevant to this application and any how the officers
concerned realizing the issue have refrained from interfering with the issue of this case which is
private and family issue.
The Petitioner is claiming the rights to the relevant land to this application as the eldest son of the
said Kamburudeni Devage Alice and which is not permitted in law as there is a nominated
successor, the 11th Respondent, and which is duly registered in the relevant Land Registry as
required by law and acquired possession of the relevant land by the 11th Respondent, to this
application after the death of her mother. There was no suggestion to partition the land
concerned by the 1st Respondent as it is obviously illegal.
The Respondents further emphasize that the Petitioner had made false complaints to the officers
concerned with cruel and bad intension to harm his own relatives. They all say that the Petitioner
is alone on one side and the others the above said Respondents are on the other side of the
conflict. It is emphasized that the complaint of the Petitioner is a private and a family dispute and
not otherwise.
Subsequent to a thorough analysis of the facts of this case, it could be revealed that the issues or
the questions of law to be determined and decided is whether the 1st Respondent has a public
duty to cancel the grant given to the 11th Respondent and to recommend the President of the
Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka to cancel a grant given after land kachcheri or due
process in terms of Land Development Ordinance, to the 11th Respondent. The other vital question
of law is whether the Petitioner has a legitimate expectation with regard to cancellation of the
grant given to the 11th Respondent and to recommend the President to cancel a grant given after
land kachcheri.
It could also be noted that Petitioner has complained in his Petition that the 11th Respondent has
violated the terms and conditions of the relevant Grant to this application. The above
Respondents deny the said violation of terms and conditions of the said Grant. Accordingly, the
major facts and allegations are in dispute.
It is held as follows in the case of THAJUDEEN VS SRI LANKA TEA BOARD AND ANOTHER (1981) 2
SLR 471 inter alia that;
"Where the major facts are in dispute and the legal result of the facts is subject to
controversy and it is necessary that the questions should be canvassed in a suit where Page 7 of 8
parties would have ample opportunity of examining the witnesses so that the Court would
be better able to judge which version is correct, a Writ will not issue. Mandamus is pre-
eminently a discretionary remedy. It is an extraordinary, residuary and suppletory remedy
to be granted only when there is no other means of obtaining justice. Even though all other
requirements for securing the remedy have been satisfied by the applicant, the court will
decline to exercise its discretion in his favor if a specific alternative remedy like a regular
action equally convenient, beneficial and effective is available"
In the circumstances aforesaid, the application is hereby dismissed, with cost

Janak De Silva, J
